posts.author: Zia_
posts.body:
(Contains a little 2024 review, as this post was originally posted in a 24/25 thread)
During the Christmas season 2023 I decided to get back to RPG Maker in 2024, so I spend a few weeks with researching, styleguide, checking out Aseprite, doing story drafts etc.
During February, there was a sale and I got RPG Maker MZ.
From there, I worked almost every day on my project. I really enjoyed the time, and also the results so far. ~35 hours of continuous gameplay are done, and I recently implemented the "final boss", which in fact isn't the final final one, as there's some True Ending bonus content to follow.
But it was an awesome achievement for me to finish this milestone within 2024.
As I don't like to stress myself with something I enjoy doing anyway, I don't have any goals for 2025, except to continue like this. When it's done, it's done. The scope is very realistic to - maybe - finish all the work on my side this year.
So some adventure awaiting might be to recruit some support this year to improve graphics and get some Soundtrack done.

posts.author: Zia_
posts.body:
My first big feature block this year is Expeditions.
In my game you can recruit a lot of optional characters. Getting specific ones can unlock expeditions they will perform on their own.
This is linked to the True Ending. I need to figure out a list of requirements to unlock the True Ending - it's harder than I thought.
I don't want it to happen on its own if you just play through the game normally. It has to be a challenge. But I also don't want the player to have to grind if they figure it out too late. An example: All your companions can build up friendship as they fight together. So it's reasonable to mix your party from time to time, if they hit their maximum. I thought, it would be nice to say, have at least 500 friendship points for the True Ending. Would make sense. But if you didn't pay attention at all to friendship during the game, you might have to fight 1000 battles just to build it up later ... So, I dropped that from the list.
But I do know, unlock and finish all expeditions will be one of the requirements.

posts.author: ZeroBreak
posts.body:
Tragic news regarding my publishing arrangements for The Story of Two as the game has been canceled by its developer. Although every effort was made to see the project to completion, progress has come to a complete stop owing to creative struggles and a lack of focus which has made it difficult for the developer to complete the project. (As a side note, I was going to post an update to the game's project page here on the forums to make the announcement, but it has either been deleted, its developer rendered unidentifiable or unregistered, or both; furthermore, all assets in my possession that are not related to development news are in the process of being deleted from my social channels as I obviously no longer have the rights to use them.)
As for actual game development, my efforts to branch beyond RPG Maker continue unaffected, and character development is also progressing. In fact, all but one main character is fully realized on my current iteration of the concept that started my journey here.
I'll start with Andrew Frostworth; as you can tell from his thermal suit, winter coat and knit cap, he's a specialist in working in environments that subject him to extremely cold temperatures.
Ra Takumen is the embodiment of the ancient solar guardian for whom she is named, and the crested headband that she wears is an indication of that. Her attire is an ancient cloak and armor design that has been handed down by her ancestors for generations.

posts.author: bgillisp
posts.body:
I'm entering Beregon's jam. If I meet GGGs timeline as well I'll cross enter it, but its not a focus.
Game: Darkmare University: Summer Camp
The premise is you are Lynn, a Necromancer who has been invited to participate in summer camp held by the university. Will you survive the week at camp? Will you make friends? Do Necromancers even HAVE friends? Or do you find love? Or just heartbreak? Find out!
So far I've made sprites for 5 of the characters (Lynn, one party member and 3 NPCs) and mapped the first two maps. I'm using Trinity DLC + Avery's RTP enhancements for this one, still looks pretty RTPish, but its not as bad as the neon green of default MZ RTP which I hate.
And a screenshot to show part of a map. You can see the ghost here as well.
I'm going to later apply a tint and maybe a fog to the map, plus most of the game takes place at night so it will not be as bright for that reason as well. But that's on the later to do list.
And yes, day 1 is you go to the beach. You got a quest to find something that is around here...somewhere.

posts.author: RCXGaming
posts.body:
My entry for the GGG jam (Pattern Breaker) is shaping up pretty well.
I've been working on it non-stop since the jam started a week ago, and every passing day has been action-packed with meaningful updates. As of posting, the completion rating on the project is sitting at 31%, which is not bad considering I'm flying solo and that number can change at any given moment based on "Oh right, I actually need this" syndrome.
The plot has a defined beginning, middle and end, the item and skill selection are filled out, the bestiary is more or less set in stone and all the mechanics are set in place. Which is huge because normally I'm stonewalled by never being able to start.
The hard part is primarily making sideview action sequences because I'm normally a front-view dev.
The latest big thing I did was working on the level-up screen:
Numbers are very small on purpose so any given equipment or armor can feel like a noted upgrade instead of "I guess I'm stronger now".
Level cap is 10, you only need 100 EXP to get to every level, and you don't learn skills via level up, nor do you gain HP, Defense or Magic Defense.
So instead you have to eat that character's favorite food to get +5 HP and +1 in defenses, as well as trade in vouchers to learn skills from the local kitsune girl.

posts.author: ZeroBreak
posts.body:
I realize that this is a cross-post from the jam discussion, but I figured that I'd put it here as well. In any case, I've done some more asset acquisitions for the purpose of setting up Genni's aquatics equipment. By comparison to her cousins, she uses a control vest that's inflated from behind as opposed to around her sides, which gives her a pair of storage pockets in their place (one of which is used to holster her oxygen meter). As well, her upper straps are chest-length with her octo line strapped to her right shoulder and a vertical, x-shaped connector for her oxygen hoses compared to the horizontal layout that Alan and Kyla use. The strap for her oxygen tank is also configured differently, as it uses thick fabric for its construction rather than the metal bands on the back of her cousins' vests. (She also has extra-large breathing regulators instead of the compact designs that are used by the rest of her family.)
As I have not yet rendered her directional sprites to MV format, I'm going to start with the overview photos that I took of her in Blender to give you an idea of how her gear is laid out.
As a side note, the motorized bodysuit that Genni wears as a child is an Overture Series 3T, while Kyla wears an Overture Series N. Both suits are designed to be as fashionable as they are functional, so there's a bit of a Ralph Lauren approach to their construction and development. (Note that I have yet to prepare Alan's sprites or debut his childhood appearance, but what I will tell you is that his suit of choice is an Overture Series 3A Mk. II.) As well, a common aspect of Overture bodysuits is the incorporation of a fully functional, QR-style "scan code" pattern into the visual design that doubles as a backhanded promotional element.

posts.author: ZombieKidzRule
posts.body:
Well, I'm still plugging away at learning Javascript and planning a tutorial series for implementing everything in RPG Maker MZ.
I've made very small progress on my Sudoku game, but very negligible. I'm still testing my new method for generating an original puzzle (works fine), but I haven't fully tested the removing a certain number of squares based on difficulty level.
But I will share a screenshot of a new project I have been planning and I finally started experimenting with to figure out concepts, mechanics, and rule testing.
It will be a D&D-style RPG with a Yahtzee-Poker hybrid as part of the combat.
Essentially, the conceptual combat loop is something like this:
Encounter Starts.
Player declares Intent from 8 possible actions (d8). This reflects what they want to do in their turn. If they end up taking that Action, they get a bonus.
Attack
Power
Defend
Guard
Skill
Move/Command
Equip/Use
Free Choice (Must get at least 3 of these dice to choose this and the bonuses/benefits are less than the other choices.)
Player rolls 5 d8 up to 3 times similar to Yahtzee.
Player decides where to put their roll on their Tracking (Yahtzee-style) sheet. This includes Reserving up to 3 Actions per sheet because the player decides it's better to NOT take an Action that turn and the player can override/replace most rows on the sheet (unlike regular Yahtzee).
Higher results mean better bonuses and benefits. Lower results mean penalties and some negative effects.
Depending on what the player chooses for the results, they can also Reserve up to 3 dice results from certain spots on the sheet. Such as Reserving the 5th dice result when selecting 4 of a Kind or 2 Pairs. These dice can be used in subsequent turns to replace single dice results, as needed, to help get a result that the player wants or to finish a row on the Tracking Sheet that is harder to get.
Among the possible benefits from higher rolls includes gaining up to 3 d8 and 3 d20 rerolls.
The final results are compared against the enemy. Whoever has the higher roll, gets a bonus. The lower roll gets a penalty. Tied rolls have no modifiers. This is mostly where the modified Poker rules come into play.
Once the Yahtzee rolling portion is done and the player has decided what Action they will take based on their ending roll results and all bonuses or penalties have been calculated, the actual D&D-style turn happens with appropriate d20 rolls. So choosing Attack as an action doesn't automatically mean that the player will hit or do damage to the enemy.
This follows Initiative order.
Most Actions use Stamina and gain XP for skill improvement outside of Level Up. Almost everything the player does earns XP to improve a related skill.
The player mostly controls when their current Tracking Sheet is completed (because they can replace most rows on the sheet) and completing a Tracking Sheet provides additional benefits toward Leveling Up.
If the encounter is still going after the D&D-style turn, the game play loops back to the player declaring their Intent for the next turn.
I envision the player having NPC party members as well but NPCs and enemy rolls will be automatic with the player's. So all Yahtzee turn rolls happen at the same time.
I have most of the rules drafted and now I just need to test them and see how they work in practice. And, most importantly, to see if the game play loop is fun or just frustrating. And that everything is balanced.
Within the rules, I'm trying to maximize the strategic opportunities for the player in decision making.
And I view the aspect that the player might not get the necessary rolls to do the Action they want as the reality in a conflict where things change and you might have to do something different than you planned.
For instance, I really want to equip or use something, but I end up deciding my best option based on my final roll is to Attack, or Move, or Guard, or something else based on potential benefits/bonuses versus possible penalties.
Any result of 1 on the 8 Action portion of the Tracking Sheet (such as 1 Attack dice) will always have penalties and negatives. That doesn't mean you can't Attack or that you won't hit the enemy.
Anyway, that is the idea behind it. Time will tell what the experience is actually like in practice.
Here is a screenshot of what I have been working on for the two days since I started the new project. This is just conceptual right now because I need to figure out where a bunch of other things would go on the screen, including the combat, NPCs, enemies, etc. These things will most likely need to get smaller.
Once I get the rules more solidified, I will make a post asking if anyone is interested in reading through them to offer their feedback and opinions.
Good luck to everyone on their projects!
EDIT: Forget to mention the d8 has Action icons instead of numbers.
